Selected Assignments & Grade Evidence

Finance & Investments

Corporate Finance

BAFI3184 · Individual Valuation Report · May 23, 2025
HD 82

Problem & Scope: Assessed DHG Pharmaceutical’s equity value and investment attractiveness using 2025–2029E forecasts.

  • Method & Tools: Built forecast financials and applied WACC/CAPM, comparable valuation (P/E, EV/EBITDA), Dividend Discount Model and market-transaction evidence to triangulate value.
  • Outcome: Produced a Hold recommendation, identifying short-term overvaluation; achieved HD 82, the highest assessment result in the course.
  • Capabilities Gained: Financial modelling, valuation, cost-of-capital estimation and investment judgement.
Why this matters: By building and evaluating valuation models, I developed the ability to challenge assumptions, compare methodologies and justify evidence-based conclusions — applied finance education reinforces higher-order thinking and transferable employability capabilities beyond technical knowledge (Parrado-Martínez & Sánchez-Andújar 2020).
Grade evidence

Derivatives & Risk Management

BAFI3192 · Team Trading Report · April 17, 2026
DI 76

Problem & Scope: Evaluated macroeconomic drivers and entry timing across 7 currency pairs during volatile global market conditions.

  • Method & Tools: Combined macroeconomic analysis, technical signals and real-time trading, supporting trade monitoring and stop-loss execution.
  • Outcome: Limited portfolio impact to approximately −0.26% while achieving DI 76.

Derivatives & Risk Management

BAFI3192 · Individual Portfolio Simulation · May 20, 2026
DI 73

Problem & Scope: Constructed and managed a high-risk US technology portfolio while balancing return objectives against downside exposure.

  • Method & Tools: Applied a top-down screening approach, financial and technical analysis, hedging concepts across forwards, futures, options and swaps, and three Value-at-Risk methodologies.
  • Outcome: Generated a 7.91% return over 13 trading days and ranked among the top 10 participants in the peer simulation.
  • Capabilities Gained: Portfolio construction, VaR analysis, hedging, risk identification and risk-return judgement.
Why this matters: Prepared me to evaluate downside scenarios and incorporate risk protection into investment, valuation and capital-allocation decisions.

Money & Debt

BAFI3273 · Individual Credit Assessment · August 22, 2025
DI 76

Problem & Scope: Assessed Mobile World Group’s creditworthiness and probability of default from the perspective of lenders and bond investors.

  • Method & Tools: Applied the S&P credit-rating framework, integrating country and industry risk, competitive position, cash flow/leverage, liquidity, capital structure and governance.
  • Outcome: Derived a BBB− credit assessment and developed recommendations covering maturity structure, covenants, deleveraging and sustainability-linked financing; achieved DI 76.

Economics

Macroeconomics for Decision Making

ECON1266 · State of the Nation Report · January 16, 2025
DI 77

Problem & Scope: Investigated how China’s property crisis transmitted into economic growth and evaluated whether monetary and fiscal intervention could restore sustainable expansion.

  • Method & Tools: Applied Aggregate Expenditure, Money Supply–Money Demand, IS–LM and Solow–Swan models to analyse interest rates, investment, output and long-term productivity.
  • Outcome: Concluded that stimulus could support short-term recovery, while technology, R&D and structural reform were necessary to reduce dependence on property-led growth.
  • Capabilities Gained: Macroeconomic interpretation, policy evaluation, economic research and scenario-based reasoning.
Why this matters: Economics study strengthened my ability to assess trade-offs, systemic risks and long-term outcomes, supporting sustainable problem-solving beyond short-term financial outcomes (Tallgauer & Schank 2024) and transferable career development across industries (Li et al. 2023).
Grade evidence

Behavioral Econometrics

ECON1313 · Individual Econometric Report · April 28, 2025
HD 81

Problem & Scope: Tested whether digitalisation influences CO₂ emissions across Africa and Asia, while examining renewable energy and regional differences.

  • Method & Tools: Built and compared six econometric models in RStudio, applying simple/multiple regression, log transformations, interaction effects, confidence intervals, t-tests and F-tests.
  • Outcome: Identified statistically significant relationships between internet usage and emissions and developed region-specific recommendations, including an estimated 0.32% reduction in CO₂ per capita associated with the modelled relationship.
  • Capabilities Gained: RStudio modelling, hypothesis testing, model comparison and statistical interpretation.
Why this matters: Prepared me to test assumptions, distinguish correlation from evidence and quantify relationships when evaluating forecasts and business impact drivers.
Grade evidence

Behavioral Econometrics

ECON1313 · Team Econometric Project · May 22, 2025
HD 82

Problem & Scope: Investigated the drivers of financial development across 81 emerging economies using cross-country economic and institutional data.

  • Method & Tools: Collected and cleaned World Bank data, treated missing values and outliers using IQR and Cook’s Distance, and contributed to OLS estimation, diagnostics and robustness checks.
  • Outcome: Identified GDP per capita, government effectiveness and nonlinear FDI effects as important determinants; achieved HD 82.
  • Capabilities Gained: Data preparation, OLS modelling, diagnostic testing, robustness analysis and analytical judgement.
Why this matters: Prepared me to work with data modelling and statistical interpretation in future financial-analysis and valuation tasks.

Community

Volunteer Experience

Volunteer Participant — Tuong Nguyen Pagoda Charity Association

2018 – Present

I grew up in a family where healthcare service, Buddhist values, and compassion were lived rather than taught. From my parents and aunts, I inherited a strong sense of spirituality and love, a belief that caring for others is part of living with purpose.

Reading Les Misérables by Victor Hugo first deepened my awareness of inequality, but my first volunteer trip to Trà Bông District, Quảng Ngãi Province made it real. Seeing communities with limited access to basic healthcare turned sympathy into responsibility, and responsibility into action.

Since 2018, volunteering has become one of the clearest ways I express who I am. It is why SDG 3: Good Health and Well-being, particularly Target 3.8 on equitable access to essential healthcare (SDG 2026), resonates deeply with me — compassion matters most when it becomes something useful to others.

Responsibilities & Community Impact

  • Scope: Supported quarterly healthcare programs serving 500–2,000 disadvantaged residents per trip across remote communities in Vietnam.
  • Method & Execution: Coordinated patient flow, medical-team support and distribution of 300+ kg of food and essential supplies, including registration, examinations, meals and beneficiary logistics.
  • Outcome: Helped raise VND 10 million for healthcare support and represented the program through an interview with Binh Phuoc Television.
  • Capabilities Gained: Strengthened stakeholder coordination, operational planning, adaptability, teamwork and communication.
Why this matters: I learned to translate compassion and responsibility into disciplined execution, strengthening my ability to work with diverse stakeholders in demanding environments.
Beyond Work

Hobbies & Interests

Hiking

Beyond the Trail: Building Body and Mind Resilience

Hiking is more than a hobby; it is a personal practice that strengthens my wellbeing, resilience and adaptability. I enjoy monthly hikes to mountainous areas across Vietnam with my friends. My interest grew after volunteering trips, as hiking allows me to reconnect with nature, enjoy fresh air and green scenery, and experience the sense of accomplishment that comes from overcoming physical challenges. Scientifically, green exercise is positively associated with mental wellbeing, while navigating changing terrain and fatigue strengthens my persistence and flexibility (Liu et al. 2026; Chen et al. 2025).

Why this matters: Maintaining composure, adjusting to uncertainty and sustaining effort under pressure.

Learning Spanish

Curiosity, Discipline & Global Perspective

Learning Spanish is a daily practice that strengthens my curiosity, consistency and global outlook. I have practised Spanish daily on Duolingo as my third language for four years. Maintaining consistent progress requires discipline and commitment, while the learning process allows me to continuously expand my vocabulary and understanding of Spanish-speaking cultures. This also supports my employability in multicultural workplaces and enhances career mobility across cultural and geographic boundaries (Tran et al. 2024).

Why this matters: Intercultural communication, self-discipline and readiness to collaborate with diverse international stakeholders.
